text:
incident-bot: ALERT — High error rate and latency on /v1/generate in us-west1 :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Symptoms: 5xx spikes, up to 12% errors; p95 and p99 latency blowups (p95 ~2.4s, p99 ~18s). Triggered by synthetic canaries and customer telemetry. Paging oncall.
maya: oncall (maya) here, ack. looking at dashboards now.
deploy-bot: Deploy finished at 11:37 UTC — service=api-service image=redwood/api:v3.2.1 (canary->prod)
sam: that timing aligns with the deploy, seeing errors start ~11:38 UTC
tony: quick metric snapshot from grafana: pre-deploy p95 ~180ms -> post-deploy ~2400ms, p99 from ~500ms -> ~18s. 5xx rate jumped to ~12% on /v1/generate
liz: CS note: incoming tickets about timeouts and gateway errors for customers in us-west1, several on dedicated capacity. estimating ~40 active sessions affected right now
maya: grabbing logs for api-service pods in us-west1, will look for signs of head-of-line or queueing.
sam: if it's the deploy we should rollback asap; starting rollback now.
sam: command: ```kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/api-service --to-revision=2```
deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by sam at 11:46 UTC — rollback rollout-id=rb-2024-11-46, expected ~30-60s for full rollback
ton y: quick check of recent PRs — v3.2.1 changed the model-client default request timeout and added synchronous batching config. could be backpressure on model-backend causing upstream timeouts
maya: I see `connection_pool_exhausted` and `upstream_idle_timeout` in proxy logs around deploy window. also a few model-backend 429s.
liz: flagging enterprise accounts: acct-redwood-alpha and acct-payments-ops show multiple failed requests. CS routed first tickets to priority support.
sam: curl health check against api-service: `curl -s -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}
" -o /dev/null https://api.us-west1.redwood/v1/health` — pre-rollback returning 200 0.18, post-deploy it was 200 2.3
maya: rollback completed at 11:48 UTC per deploy-bot. I'm watching metrics to confirm.
deploy-bot: Rollback complete — service=api-service image=redwood/api:v3.2.0, duration=120s
ton y: metrics update: p95 back down to ~210ms, p99 ~600ms, 5xx back to baseline ~0.5%
maya: good signal. marking incident as mitigated.
ryan: opening incident ticket and postmortem placeholder. need: timeline, root cause (deploy change to batching/timeout), who rolled back, customer impact, and follow-ups.
liz: customer impact notes: ~40 sessions affected, two enterprise customers with elevated error rates, CS sent initial notice. recommend follow-up outreach once postmortem ready.
sam: immediate follow-ups: revert the batching change in a branch, add stricter canary thresholds (reject if p95 > 500ms or errors >1%), and add circuit-breaker on model-backend to fail fast instead of queueing
maya: capturing traces and slow requests now — `gcloud logging read "resource.labels.location=\"us-west1\" AND protoPayload.serviceName=\"api-service\"" --limit 1000`
ryan: will own postmortem, tony to verify the code diff that introduced the change, sam to coordinate the safer rollout plan and canary gating, maya to collect logs/traces, liz to handle customer comms
maya: handoff: I'm stepping off primary oncall in 30m — handing to sam for follow-ups and verification. please ack.
sam: acked, I'll take the handoff and keep monitoring for 2 hours.
incident-bot: Incident severity changed to mitigated. Close if no regressions in next 60m. :white_check_mark:
maya: closing thread for now, will reopen if errors reappear. thanks everyone for fast response.
ryan: adding timeline and attach logs to the ticket.
